newsitem.title: USA: Fashion designer Versace shot dead in Miami Beach.
newsitem.headline: Fashion designer Versace shot dead in Miami Beach.

text.p: World-renowned fashion designer Gianni Versace was shot and killed in broad daylight on Tuesday outside his mansion on the tourist mecca of Miami Beach.
"I can confirm that he was brought here to the ... trauma centre and that he expired," Doris Perez, a spokeswoman for Jackson Memorial Hospital, told Reuters.
Police said they were seeking a white man aged about 25 who approached Versace and shot him in the back of the head at the gates of the mansion.
Miami Beach police spokesman Al Boza said Versace was shot "at point-blank range."

The Italian designer, 50, was returning to his home from a nearby restaurant on the Ocean Drive strip, a street of brightly painted art deco hotels and trendy restaurants featured in the Robin Williams movie "The Bird Cage."
Miami Beach, a narrow finger of land off the Florida mainland, is a tourist mecca and the centre of Miami's swinging fashion and music industry.
Eddie Bianchi, 50, the owner of a rollerblade shop, told Reuters he was nearby when the shooting occured.
"We heard two shots. I saw people running. Gianni was on the stairs. He was shot twice in the head. We were trying to help Gianni on the floor, but we realised it was too late."
"Gianni Versace was a worldwide personality, so for the people who work here on Ocean Drive, it's really awful."
Behind police lines, a large bloodstain could be seen at the front of the mansion. Blood from Versace's wounds appeared to have spilled and poured down the stairs.

Globe-trotting Versace, who dressed some of the world's most beautiful women, was not a permanent resident of Miami Beach but frequently stayed at the white stone mansion, the most sumptuous private residence in the area.

Neurosurgeon Dr. Phillip Villanueva told reporters at Jackson Memorial Hospital, "The patient suffered gunshots to the head. It apparently involved two gunshots to the head. He was seen and evaluated by myself and by the trauma nurse surgeon."

"He came in, basically his heart had stopped and the fire rescue team was keeping his vital signs going at this time. And indeed he had no evidence of neurologic function. He was brain dead and systemically dead at that time."
